## 1. Goal

Back the complexity table with measurements: time per decision against n for each policy.

## 2. Background

**PRD §1A rule:** nothing from "Nice to have" starts until every "Must have" row is done and the full demo path has run once end to end (K-32).

**From BLUEPRINT §3.8:**

| Algorithm | Time | Space |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heap operation | O(log n) | O(n) |
| Greedy fill, full run | O(n² log n) worst, ≈ O(n log n) typical | O(n) |
| Reservation, per trigger | O(r log r) | O(r) |
| Knapsack batch, per window | O(n² / ε) | O(n² / ε) |
| Exact solver | O(n! · n²) | O(n) |

**From BLUEPRINT §6 (Also recorded):**

**Also recorded:** running time of each scheduler per decision, to back the complexity claims with measurements.

## 3. Scope

**In scope:**

- Timing the CLI (or a C timing harness) over growing n
- Writing `results/summaries/timing.csv`
- A short note comparing growth with the complexity table

**Out of scope:**

- Optimising code

## 4. Files

| Path | Create / modify | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tools/bench_timing.py` | create | Benchmark |
| `cli/main.c` | modify (if needed) | Optional timing output (outside core/) |

## 5. Specification

Timing code never lives in `core/` (no I/O, no clocks there). Columns proposed: `policy,n_jobs,seed,seconds,events,seconds_per_event` (a new file; adding it to PRD §5 first if Ahaana plots it).

## 6. Step-by-step tasks

1. Choose n values
2. Measure with repeats
3. Write CSV
4. Compare with BLUEPRINT §3.8

## 7. Tests to write

| Test name | What it checks | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bench-runs` | Small n quick mode | CSV written with expected columns |

## 8. Acceptance criteria (Done when)

- [ ] Measured time per decision against n for each policy, written as a CSV supporting the complexity table
- [ ] If plotted, the format is added to PRD §5 first

## 9. How to verify

```sh
python tools/bench_timing.py --quick
```

## 10. Viva notes

**Idea:** big-O predicts growth; measurements show it on real inputs.
**Examiner question:** "Does your run time match O(n log n)?" — The timing CSV shows time per event growing roughly like log n on typical workloads.

## 11. Pitfalls

- Timing the first (cold) run only
- Putting timers in core/
